title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/20/2026
Reason for Admission: Severe sepsis and pneumonia.

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 78-year-old woman who presented to the hospital with severe sepsis secondary to pneumonia. During her hospitalization, she developed an acute kidney injury (AKI) as a complication of the systemic infection. She was managed with intravenous fluids and appropriate antibiotics. Laboratory monitoring showed that while no specific organism grew in cultures, her renal function showed significant improvement over the course of her stay. She remained hemodynamically stable throughout the admission. By the time of discharge, her kidney function had successfully recovered. She tolerated a transition to oral medications well and was stable for outpatient management.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Severe sepsis
2. Pneumonia
3. Acute kidney injury (AKI)

Discharge Medications:
- Amoxicillin 500mg TID
- Ceftriaxone 1g daily (complete 7-day course)
- Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily

Follow-up:
Follow-up with primary care physician in 1 week for lab work and monitoring of renal function.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/20/2026
explanations: Severe sepsis: the sepsis code A41.9, plus R65.20 because an acute organ dysfunction (kidney injury) is caused by the sepsis; no shock.

distractors.why: The sepsis caused an acute organ dysfunction: add R65.20.
